data.attorney_bio: Ryan brings over ten years of experience actively litigating a range of cases, including complex commercial claims, partnership and LLC disputes, high-stakes personal injury, professional liability, trademark, real estate, product liability, and consumer protection act claims. Ryan is just as prepared to resolve a case through an advantageous mediation or arbitration as he is proceeding with a jury trial on the merits. Ryan has also achieved winning results for clients at the appellate level, both in successfully affirming dispositive victories as well as overturning incorrect lower-court rulings. In Ryan's experience, the best asset in most legal disputes—the factor that usually determines success—is the degree to which his clients are empowered to meaningfully engage with and positively influence their case. Accordingly, Ryan firmly believes the key to obtaining positive legal results is establishing a highly collaborative working relationship with his clients to better mutually understand their case's strengths, challenges, and strategize the best path forward.

data.attorney_bio: Tina represents health care clients, including major health plans and health care insurers, in litigation matters in state and federal courts. data.attorney_bio: Rica V. Garcia is a senior associate in the San Francisco office of Baker Botts. She has experience advising and representing public agencies, nonprofit organizations, and federal Indian tribes on a wide range of environmental and land use matters. Prior to joining Baker Botts, Rica served as an Environmental Justice Clinical Fellow at Stanford Law School's Environmental Law Clinic and as Deputy Attorney General in the Bureau of Environmental Justice in the California Attorney General's Office. She also represented both public and private interests in matters related to environmental, land use, and public agencies at a boutique and midsize law firm in California. Rica graduated from UCLA School of Law with a focus on Public Interest Law and Policy and Critical Race Studies. As a law student, she worked as Chief Comments Editor for the UCLA Law Review. She also has a Master of Urban and Regional Planning from UCLA's Luskin School of Public Affairs.

data.attorney_bio: Mary Nguyen's practice focuses on estate planning, probate, and trust administration. She has over a decade of experience in drafting both basic and sophisticated estate plans, including revocable and irrevocable trusts, wills, advance health care directives, powers of attorney, and other estate planning documents. In addition, she has represented trustees, executors, administrators, and beneficiaries in numerous probate and trust administrations throughout California. Mary earned her J.D. from the University of California, Hastings College of the Law (now known as University of California College of the Law, San Francisco), where she was awarded the CALI and Witkin Awards for earning the highest grade in her Estate Drafting course. She also earned her LL.M. in taxation with highest distinction from Loyola Law School, Los Angeles, where she was a merit scholarship recipient. Mary was born and raised in Contra Costa County and is licensed to practice law in California and New York.

data.attorney_bio: Michael Sweeney is a senior associate in the Technology Transactions and Licensing Group. He advises life science companies, investors and other financial institutions on complex corporate transactional matters, with a specific focus on the biopharmaceutical industry. Mr. Sweeney represents clients in drafting and negotiating commercial agreements, including license, research and collaboration, manufacturing, co-commercialization and co-promotion, royalty purchase and sale, services, distribution, clinical trial and supply agreements. He also assists with intellectual property due diligence for mergers and acquisitions and private and public financings, including IPOs and follow-on offerings. Mr. Sweeney is registered to practice before the US Patent and Trademark Office and developed substantial experience at a prior firm advising companies and academic institutions on patent prosecution and counseling matters. He practiced at two major international law firms prior to joining WilmerHale. Mr. Sweeney also maintains an active pro bono practice.

data.attorney_bio: Laura Free is an Associate in Freeman Mathis & Gary's Seal Beach office. She practices in the Appellate Advocacy and Tort & Catastrophic Loss National Practice Sections. Ms. Free is an experienced litigator whose practice has included defending regional, national, and international retailers, insurance companies, and transportation carriers in a variety of high-exposure personal injury & wrongful death, premises liability, and products liability cases in California state and federal court. Driven by service and results, Ms. Free has worked with several of California's most accomplished trial and appellate attorneys. Her many successes include serving as second chair in a 68 million premises liability case that resulted in a complete defense verdict, securing multiple dismissals of her clients by way of anti-SLAPP motions and motions for summary judgment, and negotiating numerous advantageous settlements. Ms. Free earned her J.D. in 2016 from Southwestern Law School. While at Southwestern, she served as Chair of the Board of Governors of the Moot Court Honors Program and as an Admitted Law Student in the Appellate Litigation Clinic, where she briefed and argued a pro bono immigration case before the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals. She continues to serve as a coach and mentor for Southwestern's Moot Court Honors Program and has coached multiple teams of student advocates to award-winning finishes in national competitions. Prior to law school, Ms. Free earned her B.A. in Political Science from the University of California, San Diego.
data.attorney_summary: Laura specializes in Appellate Advocacy, Tort & Catastrophic Loss in the National Practice Sections at Freeman Mathis & Gary's Seal Beach office.

data.attorney_bio: Justin protects clients in labor and employment matters. Primarily a litigator, Justin handles the full spectrum of employment litigation from inception through trial preparation and post-trial resolution. He is especially experienced with allegations of discrimination, harassment, or retaliation; PAGA cases; wrongful termination lawsuits; and wage and hour violations. Justin regularly oversees both single plaintiff litigation and broader class action suits. He represents clients across industries, but his practice has become particularly focused on clients in the food systems sphere. Although his main focus is litigation, Justin aims to insulate clients from future problems by helping them improve their policies. He approaches each matter as an opportunity to learn and to avoid future litigation, and he works with clients to see what went wrong and how similar matters can be prevented. A detail-driven attorney, Justin always seeks to understand the exact circumstances and timeline of every case. His goal in court or in settlement negotiations is to humanize the client—generally an easy task for him, because he understands that employers are simply people. Justin came to the practice of law after seeing the powerful impact of his father's legal career. Drawn to the idea of helping people, he chose the labor and employment field after watching friends open companies and struggle to understand complex employment laws. He realized most employers have good intentions and want to do the right thing for employees, but need legal guidance in order to do so. Justin loves serving as a collaborative partner for clients, getting to know their businesses, supporting their dreams, and helping them find solutions.
data.attorney_summary: Justin specializes in labor and employment law, with a focus on litigation and providing legal guidance to clients in the food systems industry.

data.attorney_bio: Melanie M. Butler is an Associate in the Riverside/Ontario office of Resnick & Louis, P.C. and has extensive experience in employment law. She focuses her practice on employment defense and EPLI. Shortly after becoming licensed to practice law, Melanie operated a solo practice focused on unemployment and state disability appeals, plaintiffs' employment cases, landlord/tenant disputes, and consumer bankruptcy. Melanie also worked for several small firms representing plaintiffs in wrongful termination, retaliation, and discrimination claims, as well as wage and hour disputes, including class actions involving independent contractor misclassification and Private Attorney General Act (PAGA) cases. Her background representing employees provides her with a unique perspective when assisting employers in defending against plaintiffs' claims. Most recently, Melanie worked for a mid-sized firm providing guidance to employers on compliance with California and federal labor and employment laws, as well as negotiating pre-litigation resolution of legal claims. While attending Loyola Law School Los Angeles, Melanie interned at the school's Center for Conflict Resolution and served as a mediator on the Los Angeles Superior Court panel. She was a member of Loyola's team in the 2005 American Bar Association Representation in Mediation competition. As an intern for Neighborhood Legal Services for Los Angeles County, Melanie assisted victims of domestic violence at legal clinics located in various Los Angeles Superior courthouses with obtaining temporary restraining orders. During an internship with the California Women's Law Center, she visited women in prison who were seeking early release for convictions that resulted from battering and its effects under the California Habeas Project. Melanie ultimately decided to focus her compassionate advocacy towards employment law and is strongly guided by her early mediation experience in her desire to fairly and efficiently resolve disputes. Melanie is the mother of a young daughter and enjoys visiting museums and local parks with her on the weekends. She also has an artistic side and enjoys drawing and writing poetry, with her first poem published at the age of 16. Melanie is licensed to practice law in the state of California.

data.attorney_bio: Jessica Stone is an experienced litigator whose practice focuses on representing clients in complex commercial disputes and the defense of products liability, general liability, personal injury, and wrongful death matters. Having served as a member of several trial teams in both state and federal courts, Jessica is skilled at all stages of litigation from inception through trial, including alternative dispute resolution. Leveraging Specialized Legal Disciplines After law school, Jessica began her career at a respected Plaintiff's firm specializing in handling complex civil litigation, mass torts, and toxic torts. While there, she represented clients in litigation involving products liability, catastrophic personal injury, and wrongful death claims. Jessica now leverages this experience in litigating similar matters on behalf of clients in the aviation and retail spaces. Jessica is similarly able to utilize her background as a business litigator while handling commercial disputes. Prior to joining Clyde & Co, Jessica gained extensive experience litigating highly contentious commercial disputes, including corporate and shareholder disputes, on behalf of clients in the real estate, hospitality, and entertainment industries. Her previous experience also included handling intellectual property disputes for high-profile clients in the film and music industries. Jessica's unique background across these specialized legal disciplines affords her insight into the legal issues confronting her clients. Jessica leverages that knowledge to help her clients achieve their litigation and business objectives, whether through trial or strategic settlement negotiations.

data.attorney_bio: Andrew "Drew" Schaffer is a member of the Litigation Practice in Greenberg Traurig's Orange County Office, where he draws upon his deep civil and criminal litigation experience to serve his clients. Drew focuses his practice on business, commercial, and employment litigation, with a focus on complex litigation matters including multi-party and class action litigation and arbitration. Drew manages cases from inception through final disposition, including investigation, pre-trial work, witness and expert depositions and discovery, motions practice, settlements, trial preparation, trial, and appeal. Drew works closely with clients from the outset to develop efficient and aggressive strategies. Drew also maintains an active pro bono practice, largely focused on supporting veterans and their families. He is a member of the Board of Directors for the Veterans Legal Institute in Orange County and is a member of the Orange County Bar Association, American Bar Association, and California Lawyers Association. Drew is currently a Commander in the United States Navy Judge Advocate General's (JAG) Corps Reserve. Before transitioning to the Reserves in 2018, he served on active duty as a federal prosecutor and defense counsel, litigating various criminal matters and trying cases to verdict. Drew has deployed to Iraq, Afghanistan, and East Africa in his JAG capacity and during his prior service as an Army infantry officer with the 82nd Airborne Division. Drew is both Airborne and Ranger qualified and his military decorations include two Bronze Star Medals for actions in combat.
attorney_prior_experience: Mr. Schaffer focuses his practice on counseling and litigating on behalf of companies across industries in general and complex labor and employment matters. He litigates actions in federal and state courts involving a wide range of employment issues, including misclassification of independent contractors, wage and hour violations, retaliation, harassment, and discrimination. He also represents clients in matters before the Department of Fair Employment and Housing, Equal Employment Opportunities Commission, Department of Labor Standards Enforcement, and other administrative agencies charged with enforcement of labor and employment laws. As part of his counseling practice, Mr. Schaffer routinely advises companies on difficult employee relations and compliance issues, such as sexual harassment, discrimination, workplace investigations, large scale reductions-in-force, employee classification, and personnel policy development and administration. He also routinely litigates high-exposure Private Attorney General Act (PAGA) and Class Action matters. Mr. Schaffer assists clients in the drafting and negotiation of critical agreements needed during the employee hiring and termination process, including executive employment agreements, separation agreements and restrictive covenants. In addition to his litigation and counseling practice, Mr. Schaffer provides employment law expertise in connection with mergers and acquisitions, financings and asset deals. Mr. Schaffer is also a Commander in the United States Navy Judge Advocate General’s (JAG) Corps (Reserve) where he routinely advises servicemembers and military commands on a variety of issues. Prior to leaving Active Duty service in 2018 and affiliating with the Reserves, Mr. Schaffer served as a federal prosecutor and defense counsel, litigating a variety of criminal matters and trying a number of cases to verdict. In his capacity as a JAG, and his prior service as an infantry officer with the Army’s 82nd Airborne Division, Mr. Schaffer has deployed to Iraq, Afghanistan, and East Africa. He has earned the Army’s Ranger Tab and Parachutist Badge, and has been awarded two Bronze Star Medals for actions in combat and other decorations for his service to the United States.

data.attorney_bio: Natalie represents both public and private sector clients on a wide range of environmental topics. Natalie's practice includes litigation, permitting, and regulatory compliance related to major state and federal environmental statutes such as the Clean Water Act (CWA), National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA), Endangered Species Act (ESA), Model Toxics Control Act (MTCA), the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), and the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA). Natalie also practices in the area of eminent domain, and she has broad experience in both negotiating and litigating takings for public and private sector clients. Additionally, Natalie's practice includes strategic counseling and advice relating to water rights, natural resources, and federally licensed hydropower projects.

data.attorney_bio: Dylan Byrd is an associate in Quinn Emanuel's San Francisco office. He specializes in civil litigation, particularly intellectual property disputes and complex commercial litigation. data.attorney_bio: Gina Herrera represents public and private clients for their facilities, construction, and property needs. Ms. Herrera advises on a wide range of governance issues, and specializes in procurement and public works contracts, contract administration and project close-out, prevailing wage law, insurance and bond matters, land rights acquisitions, environmental compliance, and the public trust doctrine. Before joining AALRR, Ms. Hererra worked as an Assistant City Attorney for the City of Carlsbad, representing the city in construction project disputes, subcontractor claims, settlement negotiations and agreements, interagency water and wastewater agreements, and rate setting. Prior to her career in law, Ms. Herrera was a commissioned officer in the United States Coast Guard. She served as the Assistant Engineering Officer aboard Coast Guard Cutter JARVIS and later as a contingency planner and Command Duty Officer at Secor LA/LB, responsible for the maritime safety of 320 miles of coastline and ensuring the free movement of commerce through the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, and Port of Hueneme. Ms. Herrera also worked as an Assistant Director at The Energy Coalition, helping implement projects to increase the energy efficiency of public infrastructure and facilities.

data.attorney_bio: Robert K. Shawhan II is an associate in the downtown San Diego office of Klinedinst PC where his practice focuses primarily on civil litigation matters. He handles matters related to construction defect, general liability, catastrophic loss, probate, wrongful death, injury defense, medical and dental malpractice, and products liability. Mr. Shawhan is an active member of the Welsh Inns of Court and an elected Member-at-Large in the San Diego County Bar Association, New Lawyer's Division. Prior to his time at Klinedinst PC, he provided non-profit work for Nevada Legal Services, and he practiced civil litigation defense at a boutique law firm in San Diego, California and a mid-sized law firm in Long Beach, California. Mr. Shawhan was born and raised in Nevada, splitting time between Las Vegas and Minden (Lake Tahoe area). He received his Bachelor of Arts in Communication, cum laude, from the University of Southern California and he received his Juris Doctor degree from the University of California College of the Law, San Francisco (formerly known as UC Hastings College of Law). Mr. Shawhan is a former United States Professional Tennis teaching professional and was a nationally ranked competitive junior. In his free time, he likes to be outside staying active on the beach or in the mountains. In his free time, you can find Mr. Shawhan playing competitive tennis and volleyball, snowboarding and practicing yoga. Mr. Shawhan is most proud of his close relationship with his family and his extensive travel.

data.attorney_bio: Davis is an Associate in Maynard Nexsen's Complex & Commercial Litigation practice group. data.attorney_bio: Ibrahim Adwani is an associate in the Los Angeles Hub of Quintairos, Prieto, Wood & Boyer, P.A. data.attorney_bio: Andrew Gust is a Litigation associate focused on commercial litigation and dispute resolution. Before joining Ballard Spahr, he worked in the New York office of a Chambers-ranked law firm, handling complex disputes involving breach of contract, negligence, trade secrets, trademarks, product liability, fiduciary duty, and employment matters. He has litigated nationwide in state and federal courts as well as private arbitrations. His clients have ranged from startups and family businesses to high-net-worth individuals and public companies with billion dollar market capitalizations. Andrew believes an attorney's role goes beyond preparing to win at trial—it requires consistently positioning clients for the best possible resolution at every stage of the case. He approaches each motion, discovery dispute, and deposition as an opportunity to strengthen his client's position. Recognizing that every case evolves differently, Andrew emphasizes the importance of adapting strategies as facts and circumstances develop. During law school, Andrew gained litigation experience as a summer associate at a Chicago law firm and as an extern in the Organized Crime and Gangs Division of the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York. Before his legal career, Andrew worked as an Interpretation Ranger for the Rocky Mountain Conservancy, where he led nature-based programs. In his free time, Andrew enjoys spending time with his wife and daughter and pursuing outdoor activities such as hiking, rock climbing, skiing, and backpacking. He is also an avid fan of Chicago sports.

data.attorney_bio: Erik focuses his practice on privacy and cybersecurity-related litigation and regulatory enforcement actions. He also has experience partnering with clients to mitigate litigation and enforcement risks through practical, strategic compliance planning. Erik has worked with clients across industries, with a particular focus on the life sciences, healthcare, social media and edtech sectors. Before joining Cooley, Erik clerked for US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers of the US District Court for the Northern District of California. Erik previously worked for another international law firm, where his practice included US and international regulatory compliance counseling, advising on complex transactions and agreements involving novel privacy and cybersecurity issues, and incident response and remediation. He also maintained an active pro bono practice – including co-leading the firm's work with a national LGBTQ organization, counseling asylum applicants and representing a survivor of domestic partner violence in DC Superior Court. Erik first cultivated an interest in data privacy and cybersecurity while a student at the University of Pennsylvania School of Law. There, he conducted research on algorithmic governance as an affiliate of the Penn Program on Regulation. He also honed a keen interest in and awareness of the policymaking process, both as a law clerk for the US Senate Judiciary Committee and as editor in chief of Penn's Journal of Law & Public Affairs. Erik's thought leadership in the areas of privacy, artificial intelligence, public policy and legal theory has been featured in leading law reviews, including the Administrative Law Review Accord and the Washington University Law Review, among others. Prior to his career in law, Erik worked for three years in Washington, DC, as a policy, communications and fundraising strategist.

data.attorney_bio: Whitney Williams is an associate in the Labor and Employment Practice Group in the firm's Los Angeles office. Whitney's practice focuses on employment litigation, representing employers across various industries in state and federal courts, and in arbitration. She defends against a broad range of claims, including harassment, retaliation, discrimination, wrongful termination, wage and hour disputes, PAGA representative actions, and class actions. Whitney also defends employers in connection with charges and investigations before administrative agencies including the California Labor Commissioner, the California Civil Rights Department, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, and the Department of Labor. Before joining Sheppard Mullin, Whitney defended and advised Fortune 500 companies in employment disputes at a global boutique labor and employment firm and a large law firm. Notably, she also represented the plaintiffs in a landmark antitrust college sports case, securing a 200 million settlement for current and former college athletes nationwide. Whitney has represented entertainment talent at SAG-AFTRA in labor and employment-related contractual disputes and has worked in the Business and Legal Affairs Department at FOX Sports. She has also advised professional sports leagues and global social media platforms on legal risks. During law school, Whitney was an Associate Editor of the Pepperdine Law Review, Volume XLVII, and was actively involved in the Black Law Students' Association, Sports and Entertainment Law Society, and OUTLaw. Her law review article explored the intersection of employment law and sports, analyzing whether a sitting president, in his executive branch capacity, could legally influence the NFL's employment of Colin Kaepernick. Whitney took courses toward the School of Law's Certificate in Entertainment, Media, and Sports Law and served as a Research Assistant to a former Associate Dean and Entertainment Law professor. During and after law school, Whitney served as a judicial extern for the Honorable André Birotte Jr. of the Central District of California. In her spare time, Whitney enjoys fashion, exploring new cuisines, watching and attending sporting events, and spending time with her Cavapoo puppy, Wynona.

data.attorney_bio: Morgan Peterson is an associate in the Labor and Employment Practice Group in the firm's San Francisco office. Morgan represents employers across a variety of industries in litigation and arbitration in wrongful termination, discrimination, harassment, retaliation, wage and hour and whistleblower matters in both the single plaintiff and class and collective action contexts. She has experience representing clients at all stages of litigation, including through trial. Morgan also counsels employers on a diverse range of workplace issues and has experience developing and updating company handbooks and training workforces on workplace discrimination and harassment prevention. Prior to joining the firm, Morgan was an associate in the labor and employment department at an international law firm where she represented employers in all stages of litigation and provided advice, counseling, and training to employers across a variety of industries including healthcare, media and entertainment, sports, finance, and aviation. Morgan received her law degree from the University of California, Irvine, where she served as an Executive Editor of the UC Irvine Law Review and spent four semesters working in the Civil Rights Litigation Clinic.

data.attorney_bio: Henry represents clients in the food systems industries in labor and employment litigation. After earning his bachelor's degree, Henry accepted a role in public procurement with the World Bank, where he found himself frequently collaborating with legal teams. Fascinated by the attorneys' work, he chose to pursue a legal degree of his own, studying first for an LL.B. in the United Kingdom before moving to the United States, where he earned an LL.M. from Fordham University. It was during his time at Fordham that Henry discovered a passion for both employment law and litigation: as a student, he participated in the law school's Unemployment Action Center, serving as an advocate for claimants who had been denied unemployment insurance by the state. He excelled at quickly synthesizing the information in an individual case file, digging into the state's argument, and developing a strategy to overturn the initial findings. He also loved advocating for clients who hadn't known how to resolve their own cases. Upon earning his U.S. law degree, Henry began practicing as a general commercial litigator who focused more and more often on employment-related cases. Eventually, he dedicated his entire practice to the field, regularly advising corporate clients on remaining in compliance with ever-changing employment laws and defending employers in litigation. Henry is particularly experienced with cases involving trade secret misappropriation and non-compete agreements, as well as with the complex class action suits that arise from wage and hour claims—especially in California, where he is currently based. Drawn to the firm's client-focused decision to organize its attorneys by client industry, Henry joined Husch Blackwell in early 2025. As a member of the Food Systems industry group, he is passionate about collaborating with colleagues across practice teams to serve food systems clients. Known as an innovative thinker, Henry has a gift for developing new legal arguments and leaving no stone unturned in his advocacy for clients.

Rachel has also helped clients navigate complex financings, including Regulation A, Regulation "CF" crowdfunding, and Regulation D offerings.

Sanchez on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. data.attorney_bio: Narges Kahvazadeh counsels clients on navigating and complying with complex export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), and the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions programs. She brings a pragmatic, business-conscious approach to advising clients on international trade compliance issues. With substantial experience in preparing and submitting commodity jurisdiction and classification requests, Narges handles voluntary disclosures and assesses and improves trade compliance programs. She advises clients on strategic product design development with U.S. export controls in mind and regularly provides guidance on encryption controls under the EAR. She also addresses the applicability of U.S. export and sanctions laws to software deployment, cloud computing, including SaaS solutions, and offshore development. Additionally, she offers guidance on due diligence and integration efforts related to mergers, acquisitions, and pre-IPO due diligence. In response to recent shifting geopolitical alliances and evolving U.S.-China relations, Narges assists companies doing business with and in China. She specializes in advising clients on compliance with new export controls affecting the semiconductor industry and advanced computing sectors. Narges was previously an associate at an international law firm, where she advised both foreign and domestic clients on trade compliance programs, best practices, classification and licensing activities, and trade diligence in the context of mergers and acquisitions. Prior to entering private practice, she served as a trade compliance manager in the defense industry, where she focused on assessing and mitigating risks related to export and sanctions compliance. Narges is a member of the California Bar and the San Diego chapter of the Iranian American Bar Association. She is fluent in Farsi.

data.attorney_bio: David joined LLG's California office as an Associate in 2024. David has over twenty years of experience as a litigation and transactional attorney in diverse areas of law. Within the past several years, David has increasingly transitioned his private practice areas into focusing more on advocating for the well-being of families and their children with limited resources. These areas include conservatorships, guardianships, probate, homestead rights, and many other related or ancillary areas to help protect, preserve, and obtain the rights, benefits, and financial resources of those who need them the most. In addition, he is well adept in representing clients in administrative matters including mediation and other forms of efficient negotiations to help resolve matters before they escalate. However, if litigation is necessary, David is an aggressive litigator with a wealth of experience in all facets of litigation. David's clients come from a wide range of backgrounds, all of whom needed important legal services but were unable to afford the high cost of legal services that are all too common in today's legal environment. It is important to have an experienced and passionate legal advocate who can help deserving children and their families navigate through the frequently cumbersome process of seeking benefits to which they are legally entitled to receive. In this regard, David will work passionately as a contributing member of ot the firm. data.attorney_bio: Jack Jackson is an Associate in the Fresno office of Liebert Cassidy Whitmore, where he provides legal counsel to public agencies on a wide range of municipal and employment law matters. He advises clients on governance, law enforcement, disciplinary proceedings, litigation, and policy development. Jack is dedicated to helping public entities navigate complex legal challenges while ensuring compliance with state and federal laws. Prior to joining LCW, Jack worked extensively with municipalities, handling code enforcement, Brown Act compliance, and law enforcement matters. He successfully argued against the disclosure of law enforcement records in response to Pitchess motions and represented municipal clients in disciplinary proceedings before the California Department of Human Resources. Jack earned his Juris Doctor from Penn State Dickinson Law, where he was a member of the National Trial Team and received the CALI Award for Excellence in Law of the Sea. data.attorney_bio: Michael is an associate in our corporate team. He advises employers and executives in all aspects of employment law. Mike's litigation practice focuses on representing employers and employees in single-plaintiff employment matters involving allegations of wrongful termination, discrimination, retaliation and harassment, as well as wage and hour disputes. His counseling practice includes advice in connection with state and federal employment law, and he regularly assists employers with preparing employee handbooks, employment contracts and personnel policies. He also conducts workplace investigations and collaborates with human resources professionals and in-house legal teams to solve workplace issues and ensure compliance with existing law. Mike also advises founders and executives on employment agreements, severance packages, and other issues arising during and after employment. He has also served as a plaintiff's side employment litigator, focusing on single-plaintiff cases, class actions and Private Attorneys General Act (PAGA) matters. Mike began his legal career as a law clerk with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.

data.attorney_bio: Dale Bellitto is an associate and a member of the Labor, Employment, and Workplace Safety practice. data.attorney_bio: Tenzing Tunden is an associate in the Firm's Tax and Corporate groups. Tenzing advises clients on the tax aspects of mergers and acquisitions, reorganizations, spinoffs, deferred rollovers, equity financing, executive compensation structures, capital market transactions, and joint ventures. Tenzing represents clients across the business lifecycle, from formation, financing, restructuring, mergers and acquisitions, and succession planning, serving as their tax and corporate counsel. Tenzing also has an active practice focused on advising nonprofits on formation, compliance, and applying to the IRS for tax-exempt status. Prior to joining Weintraub, Tenzing worked at a tax law firm in San Francisco where his practice was focused on federal and international tax planning, tax controversy, FATCA compliance, and structuring and drafting intercompany agreements. Tenzing developed a specialty in the taxation and structuring of litigation settlements, judgments, and litigation finance. Tenzing has drafted over 100 "comfort" and contractual tax opinions for plaintiffs, defendants, and law firms in cases spanning employment litigation, whistleblower/ False Claims Acts litigation, toxic tort, and business litigation. Tenzing has also advised defendants and accountants on tax reporting and withholding obligations on settlements and judgments. Although Tenzing's practice is mostly transactional, he has extensive experience in federal and state tax controversies and litigation. He has represented clients from the beginning of the audit examination, through appeals and litigation in the U.S. Tax Court, and in negotiating settlements with the IRS and California. Tenzing has successfully negotiated and obtained full or partial concessions in cases involving residency and domicile, sales tax, 1031 Drop and Swap exchanges, and employment tax. A native of Los Angeles, Tenzing received his undergraduate degree in accounting from the University of Arizona. Tenzing received his J.D. from the University of California, Davis School of Law and his LL.M. in taxation from New York University School of Law. At NYU Tenzing was the recipient of the Deans Graduate Award and the Lewis R. Steinberg Tax Law Review scholarship.

data.attorney_bio: Vinh Le's unique combination of analytical skills and his ability to communicate with individuals across a variety of technical, scientific, and academic backgrounds makes him an effective representative for clients across a broad spectrum of practice areas. Vinh's professional life began as a research scientist at the University of Washington, where he conducted research in neurophysiology and computational modeling—fields requiring an interdisciplinary approach to problem solving. While he found scientific research intellectually rewarding, its theoretical nature led him to pursue a career in law as a better vehicle for applying analytical prowess to address real-world issues and drive meaningful societal change. Before joining Keller Rohrback's Complex Litigation group, Vinh practiced in a variety of areas after earning his J.D. from Emory University School of Law in 2019. He has served on court-appointed leadership committees for high-profile class actions and mass torts, including the Acetaminophen – ASD/ADHD Products Liability Litigation (MDL No. 3043) and the Gilead Tenofovir Cases (JCCP No. 5043). Vinh has been instrumental in developing leadership's pre-trial and trial strategies, particularly in areas of causation, liability, and notice. In addition, he handles cases involving antitrust and unfair competition, tackling issues such as anticompetitive behavior, deceptive trade practices, and price inflation. Vinh also brings significant experience in patent and intellectual property disputes and can pursue complex litigation across diverse industries. A hallmark of his practice is his ability to translate scientific concepts into clear and compelling narratives for clients and courts alike. A proud Washington native, Vinh spends his free time hiking with his wife and their dog, discovering new restaurants, and playing tennis. He looks forward to the return of the Seattle Sonics with great anticipation.

data.attorney_bio: Dustin Peterson is a results-driven attorney dedicated to assisting private and public sector clients in finding innovative and efficient solutions to complex environmental and land use challenges. Dustin's practice primarily focuses on land use and planning, with extensive experience in various related matters and entitlements, including the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), the Housing Accountability Act (HAA), the Density Bonus Law, the Public Records Act, and both the federal and state Endangered Species Acts. With a deep understanding of state and federal law, Dustin takes a strategic approach to helping clients navigate and resolve diverse environmental and land use issues. If a project is litigated, Dustin is a fierce advocate for clients and has experience defending projects in both the California Superior Court as well as the California Court of Appeal.

data.attorney_bio: Marthy Hernandez focuses her practice on Native American affairs and litigation. Prior to joining the firm, Marthy was a litigation associate in the Yakima office of a Washington based law firm where she represented tribal-member owned enterprises in all aspects of economic development and litigation and successfully defended against state civil regulation of off-reservation inter-state treaty right activities. While attending Gonzaga University School of Law, Marthy interned for the Gonzaga Public Interest and Indian Law Clinic. She also worked for the Child Youth Advocacy Program for the Northwest Immigrant Rights Project (NWIRP). While attending the University of Washington, Marthy studied abroad as a participant in the Northwest Cadiz Program in Cadiz, Spain. Marthy was the 2024 Director of the Law School Admissions Counsel (LSAC) PLUS Program at Heritage University. The Program is an innovative partnership among Washington's three law schools, Seattle University School of Law, University of Washington School of Law, and Gonzaga University School of Law, that aims to make a law degree more accessible to diverse students, especially Latino/Latina/Latinx and Indigenous students. Marthy was honored in 2024 with Central Washington Hispanic Chamber of Commerce's Award for Leadership in Public/Civil Services. Marthy is fluent in Spanish.

data.attorney_bio: Brandon Matamoros is an experienced attorney with significant experience in handling high exposure catastrophic motor vehicle accidents, premises liability, dog bite and wrongful death matters. Having represented clients on both the plaintiff and defense side, Brandon's practice now solely consists of representing the insureds of major insurance carriers. He has mediated numerous cases to successful settlement and is skilled at all levels of litigation from the beginning stages of discovery to trial preparation. Brandon's practice focuses on litigating high exposure cases involving spinal injuries and surgeries, allegation of mild traumatic brain injury, excessive pain management and inflated lien procedure costs. Brandon prides himself on helping his clients navigate the complex intricacies of a civil lawsuit while seeking a fair resolution for all parties involved. However, he is always ready to advocate on his clients' behalf and take a case to trial if necessary. Outside of his legal career, Brandon enjoys spending quality time with friends and family and is a passionate fan of the Los Angeles area sports teams, including the Lakers, Dodgers, Rams and USC Trojans.

data.attorney_bio: "I've always appreciated the intersection of medicine and the law and how the practice of the latter can improve the practice of the former. I feel fortunate to be a part of those efforts." Ask Ian Falefuafua Tapu to define how he approaches the practice of law, and the words that come to mind are "laulima" and "galulue fa'atasi." Meaning "to work together" in Native Hawaiian and Samoan respectively, this phrase captures the fierce commitment and collaborative spirit Tapu brings to his work. They are among the many characteristics that make Tapu an exceptional litigator, an effective advocate, and an attorney who impresses and inspires clients and colleagues alike. Tapu brings a wealth of diverse experience and insights to his representation of providers, organizations, and other clients in a wide range of health care litigation. Having served as a law clerk to three judges in Hawaii at the state and federal level, each with their own distinct approaches, styles, and priorities, Tapu developed an appreciation for how judges make decisions and the types of arguments and strategies most likely to create the desired impact and result. This 360-degree perspective informs his powerful and persuasive oral and written advocacy and led to an impressive record of results. Tapu's experience before joining HLB also includes representing clients in complex commercial litigation matters. As a first-generation college graduate and attorney from a large but close-knit family, Tapu intuitively understands the importance of listening to a wide range of views and the indispensability of collaboration when advocating for his clients. He takes immense pride in his Pacific Islander heritage and recognizes the privilege and responsibility of representing that heritage in the legal profession. Inspired by his grandparents and their journey navigating healthcare as immigrants, Tapu is passionate about health care law and understands the impact his work can have on patients' lives. Tapu has always been deeply committed to giving back to others, including maintaining an active pro bono practice. While in law school, Tapu interned for the LGBT and HIV Project of the American Civil Liberties Union in New York City, the Office of Hawaiian Affairs, and the American Indian Policy & Regulation practice group of an international law firm in Washington, D.C. He has also published extensively on topics related to the U.S. territories and Indigenous rights, winning several notable awards.

Laurie's practice focuses on the following retirement planning matters: Preparation of documents to implement and amend profit sharing, 401(k), defined benefit, cash balance and 403(b) plans, ESOPs, cafeteria plans and SIMPLEs Preparation and review of employee notices and communications Correction of plan defects under IRS and DOL amnesty programs (EPCRS, DFVC and VFCP) Preparation and review of qualified domestic relations orders Fiduciary duty analysis and training Preparation of plan policies to minimize fiduciary liability Preparation and analysis of employee benefit provisions for stock and asset purchase agreements in M&A transactions Resolving IRS and DOL audits of employee benefit plans Resolution of COBRA and other employee welfare benefit issues Related employer analysis and plan management Laurie also has extensive experience with business ownership planning, including the following: Formation and operation of business entities Ownership transition and succession Purchases and sales of businesses in M&A transactions Executive and equity compensation plans Stock option plans Transition planning for ownership of family businesses Laurie graduated in May 2017 with Highest Honors from Golden Gate University School of Law, which she attended on a full Dean's Merit Scholarship. While at GGU Law, Laurie won the appellate advocacy moot court competition, was a member of the Moot Court Board and was on the Dean's List. Laurie also was one of five graduating students to win the Scribes American Society of Legal Writers Award. As a member of GGU's Environmental Law & Justice Clinic, Laurie argued and won a motion for attorneys' fees in California Superior Court. Laurie was awarded five Witkin Awards for Academic Excellence and three Cali Excellence for the Future Awards in a range of subjects, including Writing & Research, Contracts, Wills & Trusts and Constitutional Law. Prior to joining Sideman, Laurie began her career with the San Francisco boutique law firm Buffington & Aaron, where she worked for many years as a legal assistant before becoming an associate in 2017.

data.attorney_bio: Ian is an associate in the firm's Energy Regulatory practice where he represents both public and private sector clients engaged in developing and operating energy infrastructure, transmission, and renewable energy facilities. He is experienced with a variety of state and federal regulatory matters related to the electric industry, including rate cases, enforcement, and compliance matters before FERC and state utility commissions. Prior to joining Van Ness Feldman, Ian served on the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation as majority staff under Chair Cantwell (D-WA). Ian worked on a wide array of policy issues for the Committee, including artificial intelligence, quantum information science, pipeline safety, surface and maritime transportation, and data privacy. data.attorney_bio: Molly Loy is an associate in the Ventura County office of the Beach Law Group. She represents drug and alcohol rehabilitation facilities, hospitals, management companies, state and county entities, schools, nonprofit organizations, residential care facilities, and other healthcare providers in actions involving claims of elder and dependent adult abuse, negligence, fraud, emotional distress, and wrongful business practices. Ms. Loy is also experienced in representing healthcare providers in regulatory proceedings, administrative law proceedings and appeals, and civil trials against the Department of Social Services and other state agencies. Ms. Loy is an experienced law and motion practitioner in both state and federal trial and appellate courts. She routinely drafts a variety of pre-trial motions, trial motions, writs, and appeals in cases involving premises liability, suicide, wrongful death, criminal conduct of third-parties on the premises, negligent supervision, and negligent hiring, among many others. Ms. Loy was also involved in drafting the motion for nonsuit, which formed the basis for the appeal in Doe v. Department of Children and Family Services (2019) 37 Cal.App.5th 675. Ms. Loy received a Bachelor of Arts from Arizona State University. She graduated cum laude from Pepperdine University School of Law. Ms. Loy lives in Ojai with her husband and four children. In her free time she enjoys running and reading.

data.attorney_bio: Andriy Zhernovey Associate Bio Andriy Zhernovey was born in Ukraine and immigrated to the United States at the age of 9. From seeing his parents start a new life in a new country, Andriy was shaped by unique personal experiences, a hard work ethic, and a deep passion for helping others. After completing his high school education, Andriy pursued a career in healthcare, earning a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) from Fresno State. For six years, Andriy dedicated himself to serving patients, including four and a half years as an ICU nurse, where he worked on the front lines of critical care through the COVID-19 pandemic. With a strong foundation in patient care and a desire to make an even greater impact, Andriy made the decision to transition to law. Andriy attended the University of the Pacific McGeorge School of Law as a full-time student, all while continuing to work as an ICU nurse on the weekends. During his time in law school, Andriy joined Dreyer Babich Buccola Wood Campora for a summer internship with Hank G. Greenblatt and served for a semester as a full-time judicial extern to Ret. Chief Magistrate Judge Kendall Newman of the Eastern District of California. It was during his internship with Mr. Greenblatt that Andriy realized how useful his background in nursing was to understanding people's injuries and in assisting them in their most vulnerable moments. After graduating with Distinction from McGeorge School of Law, Andriy proudly accepted an associate position at Dreyer Babich Buccola Wood Campora, where he now represents injured victims and their families beyond the hospital setting. In his spare time, Andriy enjoys spending time with his wife Victoria and their two wonderful sons. They enjoy going outdoors, spending time with friends, and dropping off their kids with grandparents while escaping to local restaurants for date nights.

data.attorney_bio: Nolan R. Jones has been an attorney with Dreyer Babich Buccola Wood Campora, LLP since 2016. He joined the firm in 2013 as a law clerk working for Roger Dreyer and Robert Bale on various complex cases while he attended law school during the evenings. Mr. Jones tirelessly represents the injured and their families to ensure they are made whole. Prior to dipping his toes into legal waters, Mr. Jones worked primarily in the restaurant industry from the time he graduated high school in 2005 until he began law school in 2012. During that time he worked for both large corporations as well as small businesses, and worked in all areas of the restaurant from host to server to bartender to manager, as well as occasionally helping out with the kitchen. Working in various positions in restaurants has helped him to understand appropriate standards of care in premises liability cases. While attending McGeorge School of Law, Mr. Jones took every specialty class available in Trial Advocacy, including a three week long summer seminar in Advanced Trial Advocacy. The balance of his education through law school with the simultaneous on-the-job training provided by Mr. Dreyer and Mr. Bale aided him in advancing his litigation skills rapidly before even passing the bar exam. Ultimately, Mr. Jones graduated a semester early from law school and passed the bar exam on his first try. He was immediately thrown into the fire by taking dozens of depositions on highly publicized cases. Mr. Jones has tried multiple cases with Mr. Bale, and continues to work with Mr. Dreyer and Mr. Bale on numerous cases, while also handling his own share of cases throughout all stages of litigation. As an attorney, Mr. Jones has resolved hundreds of cases for his clients whether that be through trial or negotiation. He has assisted in the continuing education of his peers with regards to California Lien Laws, ERISA liens, and Medicare/Medi-Cal lien statutes. Mr. Jones is licensed to practice law in California in both state and federal court.

data.attorney_bio: Sean D. Wisman is an Associate with the law firm of Dreyer Babich Buccola Wood Campora, LLP, who specializes in representing victims and their families in cases involving negligence, personal injury, wrongful death, premises liability, products liability, motor vehicle collisions, police misconduct, assault, and battery. Mr. Wisman tirelessly advocates for injured victims and their families and has successfully litigated close to 1,000 cases from inception to conclusion, obtaining dozens of six- and seven-figure settlements and judgments. Mr. Wisman earned a Bachelor of Arts in Business Administration from the University of Washington in 2008. He began working at Dreyer Babich Buccola Wood Campora, LLP in 2010 as a full-time Law Clerk while attending law school in the evenings at University of the Pacific McGeorge School of Law. He graduated with Distinction and dual concentrations in Business Law and Tax Law from University of the Pacific McGeorge School of Law, and has been an attorney at the firm ever since passing the California bar examination and being sworn in. Mr. Wisman is licensed to practice law in California, Washington, and Oregon. He has held Martindale-Hubbell peer- and client-reviewed ratings of AV Preeminent and Platinum Client Champion, respectively, every year since 2021. He has been recognized every year since 2019 as a Northern California Rising Star in Personal Injury by Super Lawyers, and every year since 2023 by Best Lawyers: Ones to Watch. Mr. Wisman served on the Board of Directors of the Consumer Attorneys of California in 2023 and 2024 and is currently serving on the Boards of Directors of the Sacramento County Bar Association and its charitable arm, the Sacramento County Bar Foundation. More than anything else, Mr. Wisman enjoys spending quality time with his wife and young son. In his spare time, he also enjoys golfing, hiking, camping, woodworking, and volunteer work.

data.attorney_bio: John C. Lender earned his Juris Doctor degree from Chapman University School of Law in 2002, and was admitted to the State Bar of California in 2002. While in law school, Mr. Lender worked as an extern for the Hon. Robert Alberts in the United States Bankruptcy Court, worked as an extern at the Orange County District Attorney's office, and competed as a member of Chapman University School of Law's Moot Court Board and Appellate Moot Court Board. Mr. Lender also worked as a faculty research assistant regarding federal sentencing guidelines, was a member of the Warren J. Ferguson Inn of Court, was the recipient of a Provost Law Scholarship, and received an Award for Excellence in Trial Advocacy. Mr. Lender's practice is focused on medical malpractice and general liability defense, defending medical doctors, medical and corporate facilities, podiatrists and chiropractors. Cases involve allegations of improperly performed surgeries, respondeat superior liability on the part of healthcare facilities, as well as sexual misconduct and battery allegations. Mr. Lender also represents doctors and nurses in disciplinary proceedings before their respective licensing boards, and represents psychiatric and eating disorder facilities. Mr. Lender takes a hands-on approach with each of his cases, meeting early and regularly with clients and expert witnesses to prepare the most effective trial strategies. Mr. Lender is admitted to practice in the Southern and Central Districts of California and the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, and he has authored multiple articles regarding the litigation process. As an active member of the Orange County Bar Association, Mr. Lender teaches MCLE classes for the Tort and Trial section involving subjects such as depositions, motions for summary judgment, written discovery, and motions to compel. Mr. Lender currently serves on the OCBA Education Committee, and he represented OCBA as a delegate at the 2019 Conference of California Bar Associations. Mr. Lender lives in Orange County with his wife and their three children. When not in the office, Mr. Lender enjoys surfing and playing guitar and harmonica.

data.attorney_bio: Mr. Bacon is a senior counsel with the Mastagni Holstedt law firm in Sacramento. For the past 45 years his practice has focused on representing and advising lawyers on a wide variety of matters. During that time period he has represented and advised attorneys and law firms in legal malpractice cases, ethics and risk management matters, fee disputes, fee arbitrations, State Bar disciplinary actions, and malicious prosecution cases. Mr. Bacon has also been certified by the State Bar of California Board of Legal Specialization as a Certified Specialist in Legal Malpractice Law. Mr. Bacon has lectured throughout California on a variety of topics including attorney's fees, legal ethics, fee arbitrator training and insurance coverage and served as a consultant and expert witness with respect to attorney malpractice, ethics and fee issues. Mr. Bacon is currently the Presiding Arbitrator for the State Bar of California's Mandatory Fee Arbitration Program. He has also been a member of the State Bar Committee on Mandatory Fee Arbitration since 2007, serving as the Committee Chair in 2011-2012 and Vice-Chair in 2010-2011. Mr. Bacon was an at large member of the Sacramento County Bar Association Board of Directors from 2014-2017, and he has been the Chair of the Sacramento County Bar Fee Arbitration Committee since 2010. He has served as a fee arbitrator for the Sacramento County Bar Fee Arbitration Mandatory Fee Arbitration Program since 1999, and also serves as a settlement Judge Pro Tem for the Sacramento County Superior Court and as an arbitrator for the Sacramento County Superior Court Judicial Arbitration Program. Mr. Bacon is also a member of the American Bar Association Standing Committee on Professional Responsibility; the National Legal Malpractice Data Center; the Association of Professional Responsibility Lawyers (APRL); the ABA Litigation Section, and the Sacramento County Bar Association. data.attorney_bio: Byron G. Danell has joined the firm in the Labor and Employment Department. Mr. Danell primarily defends constitutional principles and represents public sector employees in criminal defense related matters, including administrative hearings, disciplinary actions, internal affairs investigations, critical incidents, labor arbitration hearings and State or Federal cases. Mr. Danell works extensively with the Peace Officers' Procedural Bill of Rights Act, the Firefighters Procedural Bill of Rights Act, the Meyers-Milias-Brown Act and other related California Labor and Penal Codes. Prior to joining Mastagni Holstedt, A.P.C., Mr. Danell practiced law for over eighteen (18) years in Southern California. Mr. Danell has successfully represented numerous clients, including politicians, doctors, lawyers, fire and police in administrative hearings, peer to peer reviews and full board disciplinary or licensing issues. Mr. Danell has also represented thousands of additional clients whom faced felony or misdemeanor allegations, including but not limited to, capital murder, murder, vehicular manslaughter, rape, robbery, firearms, buy, dui, drugs, domestic violence, sex offenses and white-collar crimes. Early in his career, Mr. Danell worked on the defense team for a former U.S. Marine Sergeant and Police Officer. In that case, the Marine was accused of killing (or causing others) to kill four unarmed detainees in November 2004 in Fallujah, Iraq. The Battle for Fallujah saw some of the fiercest fighting in the Iraq war. Thirty-three of the Marine's fellow battalion members were killed in that battle. The case garnered world-wide exposure and was featured by our local and national media. The former Marine Sergeant was eventually acquitted after a Federal jury trial. After working on that case, Mr. Danell developed a willingness to fight against intractable organizational power and has continued to work daily to combat the errors associated with unchallenged organizational incompetence. Mr. Danell graduated from San Diego State University (SDSU) with a Bachelor's Degree in Speech Communication and Political Science and obtained his Law Degree from the University of San Diego. Mr. Danell has completed over fifty trials throughout Southern California and is admitted to practice in all of California and the Southern, Central and Eastern U.S. Federal District Courts.
data.attorney_summary: Byron specializes in defending constitutional principles and representing public sector employees in criminal defense matters, including administrative hearings and disciplinary actions.

data.attorney_bio: Timothy A. Davis is an Associate Attorney in the Labor & Employment Department of Mastagni Holstedt, A.P.C. He represents public safety employees in administrative and disciplinary investigations, hearings, critical incident investigations, and criminal defense. Timothy attended the Sacramento Police Academy in 1998 and spent over 25 years as a Sacramento Police Officer. Timothy served as a Patrol Officer, a Traffic Officer, and a DUI Enforcement Officer. Timothy served as a supervisor in the Traffic Division, overseeing both traffic and DUI enforcement officers. As a DUI officer, Timothy made over 950 DUI arrests and served as a Drug Recognition Expert (DRE) instructor and a regional expert in DUI Enforcement. Timothy was a two-time recipient of the MADD California Hero Award and a 13-time recipient of the MADD award. In 2011 Timothy received the State Award for Traffic Safety Excellence from the California Office of Traffic Safety and in 2023 Timothy received the MADD Lifetime Achievement Award. During his career, the Sacramento Police Department awarded Timothy the Life Saving Award and a Unit Citation. Timothy served for 13 years on the Board of Directors of the Sacramento Police Officers Association, including 3 years as Secretary and 8 years as President. Timothy is the longest serving President in the association's history. During his time with the Sacramento Police Officers Association, Timothy responded to countless critical incidents, represented employees in discipline cases and appeals, negotiated five labor contracts, and was active in the political process of both the City of Sacramento and the surrounding region. Timothy served on the PORAC Board of Directors for eight years, including serving two years as the statewide PORAC Treasure. With PORAC, Timothy worked on and lobbied for legislation at both the State and National capitols. Timothy served as a Trustee and consultant for the PORAC Retiree Medical Trust (RMT) and is an expert in the workings for the trust. Timothy served as a board member of the California Peace Officers Memorial Foundation for 8 years. Timothy was a commissioner on the City of Sacramento's Community Police Commission for one year. Timothy graduated from Brigham Young University with a bachelor's degree in History. Timothy graduated with a Juris Doctor from the University of the Pacific, McGeorge School of Law in 2016 and was admitted to the bar the same year. Timothy and his wife April have five children, two of whom work for the Sacramento Police Department. Timothy enjoys hiking, watching baseball, and being a father and grandfather.
data.attorney_summary: Timothy specializes in representing public safety employees in administrative disciplinary investigations, hearings, critical incident investigations, and criminal defense.

data.attorney_bio: Mark Desrosiers navigates complex land use and environmental matters at the administrative, trial, and appellate levels for public and private clients alike. His unique perspective stems from Mark's early career in the judiciary. As a former clerk in both trial and appellate courts, he gained invaluable insights into judicial decision-making, equipping him with the skills to prepare projects for potential legal challenges and craft compelling arguments tailored for judges. Additionally, his tenure at the City Attorney's Office of Glendale further honed his expertise. There, Mark managed complex land use litigation, negotiated high-stakes transactions, and played a key role in drafting ordinances that addressed pressing municipal challenges. His work reflected a deep understanding of the intersection between local governance and land use law, contributing to the city's legal and policy frameworks. Mark's practice focuses on intricate issues arising under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), planning laws, and zoning regulations. His extensive experience includes guiding General Plan updates, mixed-use developments, affordable housing projects, and public works initiatives through challenging regulatory and legal landscapes. Mark also has experience in high-profile litigation and appellate advocacy. He has represented clients in precedent-setting cases, including serving as counsel to The Regents of the University of California in a landmark California Supreme Court victory defending UC Berkeley's Long-Range Development Plan and the student and supportive housing project proposed for "People's Park." Mark has argued critical motions and cases in trial and appellate courts, including a five-day bench trial defending nearly 40 years of the City of Carlsbad's application of its Growth Management Plan. An active member of the City Attorneys Association of Los Angeles County, Mark has shared his expertise as a seminar leader on significant cases, including the U.S. Supreme Court's decision in Sheetz v. County of El Dorado. He has also authored articles for the Association of Environmental Professionals, offering thought leadership on emerging issues in environmental law. Complementing his legal acumen, Mark brings a financial perspective from his prior role as a financial analyst at a boutique real estate investment firm, where he developed sophisticated financial models for bridge loan investments in hospitality and commercial properties. This multidisciplinary background enables Mark to approach land use and environmental matters with both legal precision and a nuanced understanding of financial and development dynamics.

Mark served as counsel representing the City of Carlsbad in a Petition challenging nearly 40 years of the City’s implementation of its Growth Management Plan to development and long-term land use planning. Mark took drafted and argued pre-trial motions, including discovery motions and a motion to bifurcate. Mark was part of the trial team during a five-day bench trial with live testimony, during which Mark examined witnesses. The trial court rejected all of Petitioner’s arguments, and Mark is currently defending the City on appeal.

Guardians of the Pines v. City of Burbank, Case No. 23STCP03707. Mark serves as lead counsel representing the City of Burbank regarding a proposed project to remove roughly 119 aging Aleppo Pine trees in residential neighborhoods that represent an ongoing threat to resident’s safety and property from catastrophic failure during winter storms. Mark successfully argued on behalf of the City in opposing Petitioner’s motion for an injunction to halt removal of dozens of the most dangerous trees under an emergency exemption to CEQA, and is currently providing advice relating to environmental analysis of a proposed project to remove the remaining trees.

Represented the County in litigation over the Los Angeles County Sanitation District’s obligation to fund a regional park at the site of the former Puente Hills landfill, the largest active landfill in the U.S. prior to its closure in 2013, known as the Puente Hills Landfill Park. The litigation involved contractual permitting issues and complex infrastructure issues associated with building a park on a landfill site. Defendants filed a cross complaint alleging inverse condemnation. Mark drafted mediation briefs and was part of the litigation team which settled the case in 2021 and secured $80 million from the Sanitation District to fund the future park.

Special counsel to the Los Angeles County Public Works Department on issues relating to Amended Floodplain Maps. The litigation involved a CEQA challenge the County’s adoption of updated and modernized floodplain maps around the Santa Clara River. Mark wrote the substantive briefing in this case and secured a denial of the Petition challenging the adoption of the maps.
data.attorney_summary: Mark specializes in navigating complex land use and environmental matters at administrative, trial, and appellate levels for public and private clients.

data.attorney_bio: Zoë Grimaldi is an Associate in Burke's Litigation Practice Group working in the San Diego office. She graduated from The George Washington University with a bachelor's in International Affairs and with a minor in Arabic. Before attending law school, Zoë worked in public health advocacy and for local, state, and national electoral campaigns. She received her Juris Doctorate, with a concentration in Government Law, from the University of California, College of the Law, San Francisco (formerly UC Hastings). Zoë was admitted as a member of the Legal Education Opportunity Program—a program designed to make legal education accessible to those who have overcome educational, economic, social, or physical adversity. In addition to her studies, she was a member of OUTLaw, a student-led organization for LGBTQ law students, and the Disability Resource Program. She also served as a staff editor and was later elected Editor-in-Chief of UC Law Constitutional Quarterly. During her time in law school, Zoë gained experience in labor, employment, and administrative law as a Peggy Browning Fellow for the International Union of Painters and Allied Trades and as an extern with the U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Administrative Law Judges where she drafted an opinion addressing a Defense Base Act workers compensation claim. Zoë was awarded a grant from the Hastings Public Interest Law Foundation to fund her internship with the San Francisco City Attorney's Office. She worked with the City's Trial Team supporting personal injury, transportation, law enforcement, and employment cases in addition to representing the City in encampment resolution matters involving the unhoused. Zoë graduated with Pro Bono Honors for her work in immigration law and with the Legal Advice and Referral Clinic, administered by the Justice and Diversity Center of the Bar Association of San Francisco. After graduation, Zoë moved to San Diego and completed a post-bar internship with the City Attorney's Office in the Nuisance Abatement Unit, a hybrid civil-criminal practice. There, she prosecuted public health and safety misdemeanors and aided civil enforcement of state and municipal code violations. In her free time, Zoë enjoys cycling and high intensity interval training classes, learning to sail, and spending time with her husband, puppy, and two tortoises.
